sentences.text: Cladodus was an ancient cartilaginous fish belonging to the family Ctenacanthidae within the class Chondrichthyes.
Its teeth varied greatly in size, measuring anywhere from 2.2 to 90 millimeters in length.
These specialized teeth were built to grab prey and swallow it whole instead of slicing it apart.
A new species named Cladodus gailensis was officially described by researchers in 2021.
Fossil evidence of this genus has been recovered from locations in Scotland, Australia, and the United States.
In Scotland, specific finds include a braincase and a single tooth located within the Clackmannan Group.
This creature inhabited the waters between 379 and 227.3 million years ago, spanning the Frasnian to Carnian periods.
